adaptiveIcon.//: Matches the iOS icon exactly. Android shows only the central 72dp of a 108dp layer, so the artwork can't be dropped in unchanged — it would render 1.5x zoomed. scripts/sync-android-icon.mjs derives android-icon-background.png from assets/icon.png (the source of truth): the full iOS design scaled to that visible 66.7% with its gradient bled outward. All artwork lives in the background layer and the foreground is intentionally empty, so a launcher's parallax can't split the design in two. Run `npm run sync:android-icon` after changing assets/icon.png.

plugins.//: iOS: NO top-level image — ./plugins/withSolidLaunchScreen (listed first, runs last via withMod LIFO) replaces expo-splash-screen's storyboard with a solid-color UILaunchScreen that references the SplashScreenBackground asset generated from the top-level backgroundColor (#3A0A0A), keeping the launch flash-free. Android: an image IS required — withAndroidSplashStyles ALWAYS writes windowSplashScreenAnimatedIcon=@drawable/splashscreen_logo into the Android 12 splash theme, so with no image the drawable is never generated and the release build fails at processReleaseResources (resource splashscreen_logo not found). The android block supplies the brand mark (the masking-padded adaptive foreground) so the drawable exists; Android 12 always renders a splash icon anyway. This android block does not affect the iOS config.

Force every CocoaPods target to the app's minimum iOS version. Some sub-pods (e.g. RNSVG-RNSVGFilters) hardcode 12.4, which the current Xcode rejects (min supported is 15.0); this post_install bumps them all to match.
